Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: TeleHealth POC — where is data processed / subprocessors?

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the demo last week. As part of our security & privacy due diligence for the pilot, can you confirm a few specifics about where customer data (prompts, responses, any attached files) is processed and stored? We need to populate our vendor DD form and share details with Legal:

- Primary processing regions for inference and for persisted storage
- List of subcontractors / subprocessors that can access or process customer data
- Any cross-border transfers, and the legal mechanism (SCCs, adequacy, contractual safeguards)
- Retention and deletion: how long do you store prompts/outputs and how deletion is executed

I've attached our DD form (TeleHealth_DD_Form_2026.pdf) — if you can populate the fields or provide a short Q&A that would be great. We have an internal deadline to complete the pack by Sept 3.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Jared
Director, Security & Compliance
TeleHealth Inc.

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: TeleHealth POC — where is data processed / subprocessors?

Jared — thanks for the form and the timeline. Pulling together a concise Q&A below; attaching a CSV that maps regions to subprocessors and a SOC 2 summary for your legal team. Marissa (who owns product security) and Neha (privacy) are cc'd for any deeper follow-ups.

High-level answers (short):
- Processing: Inference compute for hosted and Dedicated customers runs in the region/zone you select. For TeleHealth POC we can scope compute to us-west1 (primary) and eu-west1 (backup) if you need EU locality.
- Storage: Persistent logs and customer artifacts are stored in region-specific object storage; by default us-west1 for US accounts and eu-west1 for EU accounts.
- Subprocessors (examples): Google Cloud (compute), AWS S3 (object storage replication), Cloudflare (edge/network), Datadog (observability). Full list in attached CSV.
- Cross-border transfers: We rely on contractual controls and SCCs where applicable; no uncontrolled cross-border replication unless customer enables multi-region backup.
- Retention/deletion: Default ephemeral inference cache is kept for immediate request routing and is not persisted long-term. Customer-level artifacts retained per your config (default 30 days for POC). Deletion requests are handled via API and on the backend we scrub KV caches and metadata; long-term object deletion follows cloud provider lifecycle + final overwrite where applicable.

Attachments: redwood-processing-map.csv, SOC2_summary_2025.pdf

If you want us to complete the TeleHealth DD form directly, we can populate sections and return it. If Legal wants specific contract language around transfers, I can propose a paragraph for review.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com

Attachment stubs: redwood-processing-map.csv (text/csv, 12KB); SOC2_summary_2025.pdf (application/pdf, 210KB)

Jared — quick answers inline, and a proposed contract snippet below your questions. I've also attached the populated DD form (separate upload) — let me know if you want changes.

1) EU-localized PHI: Yes — for customers who require EU-only processing, we offer an EU-only deployment profile. That pins inference and persistent storage to eu-west1 (Google) and prevents replication to US regions. To enable: select EU deployment in the console when provisioning the tenant or request an EU-only Dedicated instance.

2) Subprocessor access to unredacted prompts: Only the core compute and storage subprocessors have the technical ability to access raw data (e.g., Google Cloud for compute and object storage). Access by Redwood engineers is limited and controlled via just-in-time access policies and audit logs; engineers granted access are bound by confidentiality agreements and must request access through an approval workflow. For EU-only deployments we restrict support access to regional staff and route approvals through our EU data protection officer where required. Full access control matrix in the attached CSV.

3) SCCs / transfer mechanism: We use standard EU SCCs and a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) that references the SCCs and our subprocessors. I'll attach the standard DPA appendix (redlined copy) — Legal can reuse this. If TeleHealth needs company-level bespoke language, we can iterate.

Proposed contract paragraph (draft — feel free to redline):
"Redwood Inference will process Customer Data solely on behalf of the Customer and in accordance with the Data Processing Addendum. For customers requiring EU-only processing, Redwood will provision compute and persistent storage exclusively within the EU (eu-west-1). Where cross-border transfers are necessary, Redwood will rely on the EU Commission Standard Contractual Clauses or other lawful transfer mechanisms and shall list relevant subprocessors in the DPA appendix. Redwood will not transfer Customer Data for which the Customer has designated EU-only residency to third countries without prior written authorization from the Customer."

Next steps: I will upload the populated DD form to the shared drive and send Legal the DPA appendix. Marissa/Neha — please flag anything I missed from a security or privacy standpoint.

Cheers,
